newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says reaches Japan deregulation advisory pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says reaches Japan deregulation advisory pact.

text.p: DENVER, June 19 (REUTER) - The United States and Japan have reached an agreement giving Washington an advisory role in deregulation of key sectors of Japan's economy.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters Thursday that the agreement, reached overnight, would allow U.S. officials to have some input in Japan's deregulation though "bilateral consultations" on such areas as telecommunications, fiancial sevices and medical equipment.

"We've got a formal process now to go over these things with them before they do their deregulations," White House aide Dan Tarullo told reporters traveling to Denver for the Group of Seven Summit with President Clinton.
Tarullo said the agreement would allow the U.S. to have "direct,targetted input" on Japan's deregulation of those sectors.
He said that the consultations would take place both at a working level and at at a vice-ministerial level.
U.S. officials said the agreement was designed to increase U.S. market access to Japan and stressed that it gave Washington only an "advisory role."

McCurry said that Clinton would refer to the agreement in a speech that he is scheduled to deliver Thursday aftenoon before the start of the summit of the world's main industrialised nations plus Russia on Friday.
